incidents.victim: Google (insider misuse of confidential search data)
incidents.vector: DOJ and SDNY charged Google security engineer Michele Spagnuolo (36), an Italian citizen living in Switzerland, with abusing his internal access to Google's nonpublic Year in Search data — clearly marked 'Google Confidential' — to place bets on Polymarket under the handle 'AlphaRaccoon' on the most-searched people of 2025.
incidents.impact: Spagnuolo allegedly risked $2.75M across 25 outcomes the market treated as unlikely and netted more than $1.2M in profit; he is charged with Commodity Exchange Act violations, wire fraud and money laundering (combined max 50 years), and is also facing a CFTC civil insider-trading complaint. Google placed him on leave and the FBI traced his Polymarket wallet to his Italian government ID.

incidents.victim: TD Bank N.A. customers (and a second unnamed financial institution)
incidents.vector: Former TD Bank employee Cheungkin 'Kelvin' Lam (28, Queens NY) pleaded guilty to leveraging his teller-level access from January–May 2021 to identify large-balance accounts and pass confidential customer information to outside co-conspirators, then in May–August 2022 bribed an employee at a second bank to falsify records and open accounts used in further fraud.
incidents.impact: Lam accepted at least $155,000 in bribes and facilitated $3.43M in fraud losses against bank customers; he faces up to 30 years at his October 15 sentencing. IRS-CI and the FDIC OIG are investigating; DOJ used the case to flag that insiders remain the first failure point in bank AML and fraud controls.

incidents.victim: 7+ million elderly Americans (lead-list victims of Jamaican lottery scams)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data broker enabling fraud
incidents.vector: Troy Murray (57, Hickory NC) was sentenced to 121 months for running a seven-year scheme (2016–2023) selling 22,000+ lead lists of elderly Americans — names, phone numbers, addresses, ages and emails — to Jamaican lottery-fraud rings, typically priced at $500 per 100–300 names and paid via prepaid gift cards after wire-transfer services blacklisted him.
incidents.impact: The lists exposed personal data of over 7 million elderly Americans, earned Murray more than $5.2M, and produced victim losses exceeding $9.5M; he was ordered to forfeit $5.21M. His alias 'Steve Dixon' was prominent enough in Jamaican scam circles to appear in a 2022 song lyric.

incidents.victim: Education, transportation, healthcare and financial firms (multi-continent)
incidents.vector: Microsoft Threat Intelligence detailed 'The Gentlemen', a Go-based ransomware-as-a-service that uses XChaCha20 with per-file Curve25519 keys and aggressive self-propagation, spawning SYSTEM-privileged child processes to encrypt local volumes and network shares simultaneously.
incidents.impact: The RaaS program — which moved from a closed group to broad affiliate recruitment and just partnered with BreachForums to bring in initial access brokers and pen-testers — has hit organizations across North America, South America, Europe, Africa and Asia, combining double extortion with data exfiltration for public-leak pressure.

incidents.victim: US law firms (multiple)
incidents.vector: FBI warned that the Silent Ransom Group (also tracked as Luna Moth, Chatty Spider, UNC3753 and Storm-0252) impersonates internal IT staff via phone and phishing email to gain remote access, and when that fails sends an operative to the victim's office to physically plug a storage device into a workstation and copy files.
incidents.impact: The Russia-based group, active since 2022 with more than 100 claimed attacks, has surged activity in recent months against US law firms — exfiltrating client data via WinSCP or hidden Rclone to Google Drive, OneDrive or USB drives — and is escalating to in-person visits, an unprecedented step in the data-extortion ecosystem. Legal services was the fourth most-targeted ransomware sector in Q1 2026.

incidents.victim: Stark Industries Solutions / MIRhosting / WorkTitans (Netherlands hosting infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crime investigators (FIOD) arrested MIRhosting owner Andrey Nesterenko (39) and Amsterdam-based Youssef Zinad (57) on May 18 for violating EU sanctions by providing connectivity to entities hosting Russia-linked cyber and influence operations.
incidents.impact: FIOD raided three businesses and two data centres in Enschede, Almere, Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk, seizing laptops, phones and more than 800 servers; customer data on those servers was lost. The seizure cuts off Stark Industries' last major upstream provider after May 2025 EU sanctions against PQHosting, and follows reporting that WorkTitans/MIRhosting carried the heaviest pro-Russian DDoS traffic against Danish government bodies during the November 2025 municipal elections.

incidents.victim: AFC Ajax (Dutch football club, 300,000+ supporters)
incidents.vector: Dutch police arrested a 35-year-old man in Buren, suspected of repeatedly entering Ajax's computer systems after exploiting an unpatched vulnerability disclosed in March; investigators seized multiple digital storage devices during the raid.
incidents.impact: Ajax originally said only a few hundred emails and limited data of stadium-banned individuals were exposed, but Dutch broadcaster RTL reported the breach potentially exposed personal information of more than 300,000 registered supporters and could have affected over 42,000 season tickets, with the attacker also able to transfer tickets and alter stadium-ban records.

incidents.victim: Charter Communications (US telecommunications)
incidents.vector: Charter confirmed a security breach after the ShinyHunters group listed the company on its dark-web leak portal; specifics on the intrusion vector and scope of stolen data have not been publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Confirmation places another major US carrier on ShinyHunters' growing victim list following the group's SaaS- and identity-focused extortion sprees; the FBI has separately advised victims not to pay ShinyHunters demands.

incidents.victim: French mayoral candidates (Marseille, Toulouse, Roubaix)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — foreign influence operation under investigation
incidents.vector: Paris prosecutors opened a foreign-interference probe (suspected espionage, election fraud via false news, and online incitement) into a coordinated digital smear campaign that used deceptive websites, fake social-media accounts and disparaging ads against La France Insoumise candidates Sébastien Delogu (Marseille), François Piquemal (Toulouse) and David Guiraud (Roubaix); separately, French authorities are investigating Israeli influence firm BlackCore for possible involvement.
incidents.impact: A specialized national cyber-police unit is now consolidating evidence with parallel probes in Marseille and Toulouse; BlackCore scrubbed its online presence after Reuters inquiries. The case is the most prominent suspected foreign-interference operation against a French political party since 2024 and tests French foreign-interference law, which only criminalises action commissioned by a foreign state.

incidents.victim: Latin American government agencies (Uruguay's Antel, 25+ Mexican agencies, Colombia health ministry, Argentina's Grupo Petersen)
incidents.vector: Regional groups including La Pampa Leaks, Chronus Group and Bashe (APT73) are pivoting from ransomware encryption to 'pure data extortion' against public-sector targets — La Pampa Leaks claimed compromise of Uruguay's government-sponsored Antel identity service and monetised it as a citizen-lookup service; Chronus Group claimed data from 25 Mexican agencies; Colombia's health ministry absorbed 23M attempted attacks in March; and Bashe claimed Argentina's Grupo Petersen.
incidents.impact: Public administration was the most-breached sector in the region (21%, 543 breaches in 12 months per Bitsight); attackers weaponise local breach-notification regimes and political consequences to pressure agencies to pay, with Peru, Mexico and Brazil all in the world's top-10 most-targeted nations.

incidents.victim: Lithuania state property registry
incidents.vector: Attackers used compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorised to access land and real-estate data to enter Lithuania's state registry and exfiltrate records.
incidents.impact: About 600,000 records were stolen, including property information, owners' real names, cadastral information and other real-estate-specific details; the incident again highlights the cross-agency credential-reuse risk in shared government data platforms.

incidents.victim: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
incidents.vector: Iranian operators using the fake-hacktivist persona 'Ababil of Minab' breached LACMTA in mid-March, then used scripts and hands-on-keyboard actions across virtualization, storage and backup infrastructure to wipe databases, virtual machines and storage volumes.
incidents.impact: LACMTA data was exfiltrated and infrastructure was destroyed to deny remediation; Israeli researchers at Gambit Security tied 'Ababil of Minab' to Iran's MOIS via forensic links to prior Iran-attributed activity. The same persona has hit organisations in Israel (media and education), Turkey (insurance) and Saudi Arabia, and is part of the broader MOIS pattern that also produced the March attack on medical device maker Stryker.

incidents.victim: KnowledgeDeliver LMS customers (Japan-focused learning management system)
incidents.vector: An unknown threat actor exploited CVE-2026-5426 as a zero-day, abusing identical hardcoded ASP.NET machineKey values shipped in KnowledgeDeliver's vendor-supplied web.config before Feb. 24, 2026 to craft signed __VIEWSTATE payloads that achieved unauthenticated RCE on any internet-facing instance.
incidents.impact: On at least one Mandiant-investigated victim, the attacker dropped the in-memory BLUEBEAM (Godzilla) .NET web shell inside w3wp.exe, granted Everyone full access to the web root, modified application JavaScript to push a fake 'security authentication plugin', and ultimately delivered a Cobalt Strike BEACON keyed to the victim's organisation name — a watering-hole-style chain affecting users of any compromised LMS instance.

incidents.victim: US Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A Nightwing contractor administering CISA's code platform created a public GitHub repo called 'Private-CISA' in November 2025 and intentionally disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protection, exposing AWS GovCloud admin keys, plaintext passwords for dozens of internal CISA systems, and an RSA private key for a CISA-IT GitHub app with full access to every repo in the CISA-IT organisation.
incidents.impact: More than a week after notification CISA was still rotating leaked credentials; Senator Maggie Hassan and Reps. Bennie Thompson and Delia Ramirez demanded answers, warning the exposure handed China, Russia and Iran a roadmap into federal networks during a period of major CISA workforce cuts. TruffleHog's creator confirmed CISA only revoked the GitHub app key after additional notification on May 20.

incidents.victim: Kimwolf DDoS botnet (millions of IoT devices)
incidents.vector: Canadian police arrested Jacob Butler ('Dort'), 23, of Ottawa on a US extradition warrant; he allegedly built and rented an IoT botnet that enslaved millions of cameras, photo frames and similar devices, generating record DDoS attacks measured near 30 Tbps including hits against US Department of Defense IP ranges.
incidents.impact: Some victims incurred losses exceeding $1M and the botnet issued over 25,000 attack commands; March 19 takedowns dismantled the technical infrastructure of Kimwolf and three competing botnets (Aisuru, JackSkid, Mossad). Butler also faces charges for swatting attacks against researchers who helped unmask him.

incidents.victim: Wahlap (Chinese game-arcade maker, ~19 million customers)
incidents.vector: Wahlap left an Elasticsearch database exposed on the public internet without authentication for at least two months, leaking customer records tied to WeChat accounts.
incidents.impact: Personal details — including phone numbers and full names — of nearly 19 million customers were publicly accessible until the server was secured; one of the largest exposures of Chinese consumer data so far this year.

incidents.victim: Government of the Northern Mariana Islands (US territory)
incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted the email servers of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands; officials have not yet characterised the incident as ransomware or otherwise.
incidents.impact: The disruption is expected to slow administrative operations across the territorial government; recovery timeline and data-loss scope remain undisclosed.

incidents.victim: Bluesky users (account takeovers for disinformation)
incidents.vector: Russian disinformation group Matryoshka has been hijacking Bluesky accounts since April to post pro-Kremlin and anti-Ukraine propaganda; the platform has been progressively suspending compromised accounts until owners can resecure them.
incidents.impact: Demonstrates Matryoshka's expansion beyond X and Telegram into newer decentralised platforms; combined with Russian Signal/WhatsApp phishing campaigns against EU and US officials, signals broader Kremlin influence pressure on Western digital ecosystems.

incidents.victim: NYC Health + Hospitals (1.8+ million patients)
incidents.vector: Attackers stole medical data and biometric information — including fingerprints and palm prints — from NYC Health + Hospitals; the public hospital system disclosed the incident this week.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people had medical records and biometric identifiers exposed; biometric exposure is uniquely severe because fingerprints and palm prints cannot be re-issued, creating lifetime fraud risk for victims and making this one of the most sensitive US healthcare breaches of 2026.

incidents.victim: GitHub (Microsoft subsidiary)
incidents.vector: A GitHub employee installed the Nx Console VS Code extension, which had been compromised during the prior TanStack supply-chain attack; the malicious extension was used to exfiltrate over 3,800 internal GitHub code repositories that were later offered for sale on a hacking forum.
incidents.impact: GitHub is rotating critical secret tokens to prevent further access; the incident is notable because the breach chain traversed Microsoft's own VSCode extension marketplace, hosted by Microsoft, exploited a developer at Microsoft's GitHub subsidiary, and was enabled by the same Shai-Hulud/TanStack worm activity that also hit OpenAI and Grafana.

incidents.victim: 7-Eleven (US retail)
incidents.vector: 7-Eleven disclosed an April intrusion to US authorities after ShinyHunters listed the company on its dark-web leak portal; the company has not publicly detailed the initial access vector.
incidents.impact: Adds another major US retailer to the ShinyHunters victim list; specific data categories and customer-record counts remain undisclosed pending regulatory notifications.

incidents.victim: GitHub repositories (5,500+) via 'Megalodon' supply chain attack
incidents.vector: On May 18 a six-hour automated campaign codenamed 'Megalodon' used dummy accounts and forged author identities to push 5,718 malicious commits into 5,561 GitHub repositories, injecting GitHub Actions workflows that exfiltrate CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials, SSH keys, OpenID Connect tokens and source-code secrets.
incidents.impact: A second-stage payload replaces existing workflows with a dormant 'workflow-dispatch' backdoor that produces no visible CI runs; the incident overlaps in tradecraft with TeamPCP's Shai-Hulud worm (whose source was open-sourced May 13) and is part of a multi-week wave of GitHub Actions–based supply chain attacks.

incidents.victim: Grafana Labs (DevOps / observability)
incidents.vector: Grafana traced its breach to the same compromised TanStack supply-chain incident that hit GitHub: attackers stole the company's GitHub repositories after a developer was caught by the Mini Shai-Hulud worm, then sent a ransom note demanding payment under threat of public release.
incidents.impact: Grafana publicly refused to pay, citing the FBI's industry alert against payment; the CoinbaseCartel group claimed responsibility. The incident chains directly into the broader OpenAI / GitHub / npm exposures driven by the TanStack / Shai-Hulud worm family.

incidents.victim: US gas-station fuel infrastructure (automatic tank gauges)
incidents.vector: Suspected Iranian operators reached internet-exposed automatic tank gauges (ATGs) at US gas stations that were left online without passwords, modifying fuel-level readings on the devices.
incidents.impact: No fuel-system accident has been reported, but the targeting pattern aligns with the active CISA AA26-097A advisory on Iranian-affiliated campaigns against US OT in critical infrastructure (Rockwell, Allen-Bradley and Unitronics PLCs in water, energy and municipal targets), and validates Iran-MOIS continued probing of US OT during the post-Feb. 28 US–Israel–Iran kinetic conflict.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations in US, UK, Australia (M365/Okta tenants)
incidents.vector: Threat actor UNC6671 ('BlackFile') runs high-volume voice phishing against employees' personal phones, posing as IT for a passkey/MFA migration and steering them to lookalike SSO portals on enrollms[.]com, passkeyms[.]com and setupsso[.]com to harvest credentials and MFA codes in real time via an adversary-in-the-middle proxy.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group says dozens of organisations have been compromised and had M365, SharePoint, OneDrive, Zendesk and Salesforce data exfiltrated for extortion — in one case over a million files from a single SharePoint tenant via python-requests scripts. UNC6671 has at times misused the ShinyHunters brand to add credibility to extortion threats and now runs a dedicated 'BlackFile' data leak site, with escalation tactics including swatting executives.
